I only set the bot to utilized .5 though, so you've got to calculate that into what I've made in 29 days. This is a 29 days ending balance. 10.62. The bot is very effective at front running. When you unzip it, these will be the files you have. In this video I'll put the link down in the description on where in Github to get the bot. The files you have to focus on configure are js. We're going to open that one up here. You're going to have to configure your settings in here. The wallet addresses you want to use and the private key address you provided. If you have a wallet that does not provide easily access to your private keys like a hardware wallet you can put your wallet seat in here. Then you have the Networks. I used 1 Eth but you can always use 2 for BNB and 3 for Polygon and this is basically the settings I set for the 30 days. The point 5 I left at .5 Ethereum and that's what the Frontrunner bot will utilize whatever you have the max amount in right there. Now, this is another optional thing, I did not do this but, if you wanted to front run a Pacific token, you can put the tokens address right here I haven't tested this, but this is an optional thing that this bot I guess provides. So I'm actually gonna actually put in my give an example now this address in private key don't bother trying to copy it it will never have anything in it this is just a one I made just for the video and And this is the private key, so the private key goes right here See how I leave the princesses in there. So I have the public wall address and the private key for this wall address in here. Network set to 1 Max spin to .5 I'm going to go to save. Oh, another thing I should explain, the transaction hash, anytime the bot makes a transaction, it will be saved in this file here, so you can always go back and review it. So once we have the config.js saved we can go down to index.HTML, we're going to right-click, and we're going to go as open with. HTML we're going to right click and we're going to go as open with and we're going to open with Firefox. And it'll tell you you're starting. If I re-bot and you threw up an error because it's going to be looking for a front-run value of 0.5 in my ether balance of the wallet I provided has zero so it knows hey, we can't really do anything with that but if I had the balance in there would be telling me starting front running looking for front-running opportunities and that is basically how simple that is to configure this Bot. it's highly effective and super simple to run. I hope you like my video and i hope this video helps you out. Please leave me a thumbs up. And please subscribe for more videos. Thank you for watching.

textual.limitations: The records do not establish the currency or value of 10.62, verify the transaction history, or establish that other users would obtain the same result.

textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether any real viewer submitted credentials, whether credentials were transmitted externally, or whether any funds were lost.

It directs viewers to obtain the bot from GitHub, configure wallet credentials and run it, while describing the bot as "highly effective" and "super simple to run."
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S02 fits because the video links a trading/MEV bot to claimed profits and gives operational instructions for configuring and running it. The promotional return demonstration and encouragement to download and deploy the bot distinguish it from neutral discussion of front-running technology.
